A textual note. Later manuscripts (followed by the KJV, “the Lord added to the church daily such as should be saved”) add “to the church”. The earliest read “added to their number” (literally “together”).

For worship. Pray that your church will be marked by gladness, generosity and growth that only the Lord can give.
verseByVerse.note: The believers still worshipped at the temple while meeting in homes.

2.theology: The Sovereignty of God at the Cross. Acts 2:23 is the Reformed doctrine of divine sovereignty distilled to a sentence. The cross happened “according to the definite plan and foreknowledge of God.” The “definite plan” is God’s eternal counsel, his settled, unalterable purpose. This is not foreknowledge in the Arminian sense of God merely looking ahead and seeing what humans would choose. This is foreordination: God planned the cross before the world began (1 Peter 1:20, Revelation 13:8). Total depravity and sovereign grace appear in one verse: the guilt is wholly human, the purpose is wholly divine. The cross is the intersection of man’s worst deed and God’s greatest gift.
2.examples:
Then: The feast of Pentecost was transformed on this day from an agricultural harvest festival into the birthday of the church. Devout Jews from fifteen regions of the empire heard the mighty works of God proclaimed in their mother tongues and were cut to the heart. The harvest that day was three thousand souls.

Now: Every Lord’s Day is a Pentecost echo. The same Spirit, the same Word, the same call to repentance — and the same Lord who adds to his church those who are being saved. The question for every preacher and every congregation is whether we are as devoted to the apostles’ teaching, the fellowship, the breaking of bread, and the prayers as that first gathering was. The form has not changed. The power has not diminished.

3.title: The Lame Man and the Living Lord
3.text: <sup>1</sup>Now Peter and John were going up to the temple at the hour of prayer, the ninth hour. <sup>2</sup>And a man lame from birth was being carried, whom they laid daily at the gate of the temple that is called the Beautiful Gate to ask alms of those entering the temple. <sup>3</sup>Seeing Peter and John about to go into the temple, he asked to receive alms. <sup>4</sup>And Peter directed his gaze at him, as did John, and said, “Look at us.” <sup>5</sup>And he fixed his attention on them, expecting to receive something from them. <sup>6</sup>But Peter said, “I have no silver and gold, but what I do have I give to you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, rise up and walk!” <sup>7</sup>And he took him by the right hand and raised him up, and immediately his feet and ankles were made strong. <sup>8</sup>And leaping up, he stood and began to walk, and entered the temple with them, walking and leaping and praising God. <sup>9</sup>And all the people saw him walking and praising God, <sup>10</sup>and recognized him as the one who sat at the Beautiful Gate of the temple, asking for alms. And they were filled with wonder and amazement at what had happened to him. <sup>11</sup>While he clung to Peter and John, all the people, utterly astounded, ran together to them in the portico called Solomon’s. <sup>12</sup>And when Peter saw it he addressed the people: “Men of Israel, why do you wonder at this, or why do you stare at us, as though by our own power or piety we have made him walk? <sup>13</sup>The God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, the God of our fathers, glorified his servant Jesus, whom you delivered over and denied in the presence of Pilate, when he had decided to release him. <sup>14</sup>But you denied the Holy and Righteous One, and asked for a murderer to be granted to you, <sup>15</sup>and you killed the Author of life, whom God raised from the dead. To this we are witnesses. <sup>16</sup>And his name—by faith in his name—has made this man strong whom you see and know, and the faith that is through Jesus has given the man this perfect health in the presence of you all. <sup>17</sup>“And now, brothers, I know that you acted in ignorance, as did also your rulers. <sup>18</sup>But what God foretold by the mouth of all the prophets, that his Christ would suffer, he thus fulfilled. <sup>19</sup>Repent therefore, and turn back, that your sins may be blotted out, <sup>20</sup>that times of refreshing may come from the presence of the Lord, and that he may send the Christ appointed for you, Jesus, <sup>21</sup>whom heaven must receive until the time for restoring all the things about which God spoke by the mouth of his holy prophets long ago. <sup>22</sup>Moses said, ‘The Lord God will raise up for you a prophet like me from your brothers. You shall listen to him in whatever he tells you. <sup>23</sup>And it shall be that every soul who does not listen to that prophet shall be destroyed from the people.’ <sup>24</sup>And all the prophets who have spoken, from Samuel and those who came after him, also proclaimed these days. <sup>25</sup>You are the sons of the prophets and of the covenant that God made with your fathers, saying to Abraham, ‘And in your offspring shall all the families of the earth be blessed.’ <sup>26</sup>God, having raised up his servant, sent him to you first, to bless you by turning every one of you from your wickedness.”
3.overview:
Luke now shows one of the “wonders and signs” of 2:43 in detail. Peter and John go up to the temple for the afternoon prayer, at three o’clock, when the evening sacrifice was offered. At the gate called Beautiful sits a man lame from birth, over forty years old (4:22), carried there daily to beg. Peter has no money, but in the name of Jesus of Nazareth tells him to walk, and the man leaps up and goes into the temple courts walking, leaping and praising God, a living fulfilment of Isaiah’s promise that the lame would leap like a deer when God came to save.

A crowd gathers at Solomon’s Portico, and Peter preaches his second sermon. The healing was not their power but Jesus’ name. The God of Abraham has glorified his Servant Jesus, whom they handed over and disowned before Pilate, asking for a murderer instead and killing the Author of life; but God raised him. They acted in ignorance, yet God used it to fulfil what the prophets foretold, that the Messiah would suffer. So they must repent and turn back, so that their sins may be wiped out, refreshing may come from the Lord, and he may send the Messiah, who must remain in heaven until the time when God restores everything. Jesus is the prophet like Moses whom everyone must hear, and the offspring of Abraham through whom all nations will be blessed; God sent him first to Israel, to bless them by turning them from their wickedness.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 1–10 — The Healing at the Beautiful Gate
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: One afternoon at three, the hour of prayer, Peter and John were going up to the temple. A man lame from birth was being carried to the temple gate called Beautiful, where he was put every day to beg from those going into the temple courts. When he saw Peter and John about to enter, he asked them for money. Peter looked straight at him, as did John, and said, “Look at us!” The man gave them his attention, expecting a gift. Peter said he had no silver or gold, but what he had he would give: “In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, walk.” Taking him by the right hand, Peter helped him up, and at once his feet and ankles became strong. He jumped to his feet, began to walk, and went with them into the temple courts, walking, jumping and praising God. All the people saw him and recognised him as the man who used to sit begging at the Beautiful Gate, and they were filled with wonder and amazement at what had happened.
verseByVerse.theology:
Signs, and What They Are Signs Of

The healings in Acts are called signs, and a sign is not the destination; it is a board at the roadside with the name of the destination written on it. These are not displays of power for their own sake, and they are certainly not the working of impersonal forces — Luke will show us in this same book what happens when men try to use the name as a technique (19:13–16). They are the personal act of a risen King through men he has authorised, and what they point to is the repair of a world that has been broken since Eden. A man's ankles are made whole in the middle of Jerusalem, and the thing being said is about everything: a day is coming when the whole creation will be put right, and here is a down payment on it, walking about in the temple courts and making a good deal of noise. Reformed theology has also read the apostolic signs as authenticating the apostolic message, which is why Scripture ties them so closely to the apostles themselves, and why the long argument over whether such things continue is an argument about their function and never about whether God is able.
verseByVerse.examples: Then: The man asked for alms and got his legs. But Luke is careful about what else he got: he went into the temple, through the gate that had been the limit of his days. The gate he sat at was the boundary of his whole life, and he had spent forty years on the wrong side of it with his hand out. He received his body back, and his place with it. Now: The church still meets people asking for the small thing because it is the only thing they know how to ask for, and it still has no silver worth mentioning. What it has is a name. The temptation in every generation is to be embarrassed by that and to offer something more respectable instead.

verseByVerse.quote: Now Peter and John were going up to the temple at the hour of prayer, the ninth hour. And a man lame from birth was being carried, whom they laid daily at the gate of the temple that is called the Beautiful Gate to ask alms of those entering the temple.
verseByVerse.commentary:
One day Peter and John were going up to the temple at the time of prayer, at three in the afternoon. Now a man who was lame from birth was being carried to the temple gate called Beautiful, where he was put every day to beg from those going into the temple courts.

The hour of prayer. The temple had set times of prayer, linked with the morning and evening sacrifices. At the ninth hour, about 3 p.m., the evening sacrifice was offered and incense burned (Luke 1:10). The apostles still kept Jewish prayer times.

Peter and John. Often together (Luke 22:8; John 20:2–8; Acts 8:14). Two witnesses.

Lame from birth. More than forty years old (4:22). No natural cure was possible.

The Beautiful Gate. Probably the Nicanor Gate, between the Court of the Gentiles and the Court of the Women, made of gleaming Corinthian bronze; Josephus says it far surpassed the gates plated with silver and gold. A good place to beg: worshippers going to pray were in a giving mood.

On a Tuesday. Peter and John had their routine of prayer, and God interrupted it with an opportunity. Keep your habits, and watch for interruptions.
verseByVerse.note: The ESV notes that the ninth hour was about 3 p.m., the time of the afternoon sacrifice and prayer. The Beautiful Gate is not named elsewhere; it was probably a great bronze gate into the temple courts.

parallels.desc: the evening offering

verseByVerse.quote: Seeing Peter and John about to go into the temple, he asked to receive alms.
verseByVerse.commentary:
When he saw Peter and John about to enter, he asked them for money.

Alms. Giving to the poor was a central duty of Jewish piety (Matthew 6:2–4). Beggars sat at gates and on routes to worship.

His horizon. He asked for what he expected: a coin. God had something far greater.

On a Tuesday. Are you asking God only for small things?
verseByVerse.note: Beggars sat where worshippers passed, since giving alms was a religious duty.

verseByVerse.quote: And Peter directed his gaze at him, as did John, and said, "Look at us." And he fixed his attention on them, expecting to receive something from them.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Peter looked straight at him, as did John. Then Peter said, “Look at us!” So the man gave them his attention, expecting to get something from them.

Eye contact. Most people avoided looking at beggars. Peter and John looked at him as a person.

Look at us. Peter wants his full attention for what is about to happen.

On a Tuesday. When you pass a homeless person, look at them. Treat them as a person made in God’s image, whatever else you do.

verseByVerse.quote: But Peter said, "I have no silver and gold, but what I do have I give to you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, rise up and walk!" And he took him by the right hand and raised him up, and immediately his feet and ankles were made strong.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Then Peter said, “Silver or gold I do not have, but what I do have I give you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, walk.” Taking him by the right hand, he helped him up, and instantly the man’s feet and ankles became strong.

No silver and gold. The apostles were poor. The church’s riches were not money but Christ. A story is told that Thomas Aquinas, visiting the pope, was shown the papal treasures. “You see, the church can no longer say, ‘Silver and gold I have none,’” the pope remarked. “No,” Aquinas replied, “and neither can she say, ‘Rise up and walk.’”

In the name. By Jesus’ authority and power, not Peter’s. Not a magic formula, as the sons of Sceva discovered when they tried to use it without faith (19:13–16).

Took him by the hand. Practical help and touch, like Jesus (Mark 1:31).

Immediately. No gradual recovery; the muscles needed no rehabilitation.

A textual note. Many manuscripts (followed by the KJV, “rise up and walk”) read “rise up and walk”; some important early ones have simply “walk”. The meaning is the same.

On a Tuesday. You may not have money to give, but you can give Christ: a word of the gospel, a prayer, practical help in his name.
verseByVerse.note: “In the name of” means by his authority and power.

verseByVerse.quote: And leaping up, he stood and began to walk, and entered the temple with them, walking and leaping and praising God.
verseByVerse.commentary:
He jumped to his feet and began to walk. Then he went with them into the temple courts, walking and jumping and praising God.

Leaping. Isaiah prophesied that when God came to save, “then shall the lame man leap like a deer” (Isaiah 35:6). The messianic age has come.

Into the temple. Disabled people may have been kept from the inner courts (compare 2 Samuel 5:8; Leviticus 21:18 for priests). Now he enters for the first time, praising God.

Praising God. Not Peter. He knew who healed him.

For worship. When God answers prayer or rescues you, praise him publicly.

parallels.desc: then shall the lame man leap like a deer

verseByVerse.quote: And all the people saw him walking and praising God, and recognized him as the one who sat at the Beautiful Gate of the temple, asking for alms. And they were filled with wonder and amazement at what had happened to him.
verseByVerse.commentary:
When all the people saw him walking and praising God, they recognised him as the same man who used to sit begging at the temple gate called Beautiful, and they were filled with wonder and amazement at what had happened to him.

Recognised. Undeniable: everyone knew him (4:16).

Wonder. A miracle is a sign that points to something. Peter will explain what.

On a Tuesday. A changed life is hard to argue with. Let your life be a sign to people who know you.

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: While the man held on to Peter and John, the astonished crowd ran to them at Solomon’s Colonnade. Peter asked why they were surprised and why they stared as if he and John had made the man walk by their own power or godliness. The God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob had glorified his servant Jesus, whom they handed over and rejected before Pilate when Pilate had decided to release him. They disowned the Holy and Righteous One and asked for a murderer instead; they killed the author of life, but God raised him from the dead, and the apostles are witnesses. By faith in Jesus’ name this man, whom they know, has been made strong; the faith that comes through Jesus has given him complete healing. Peter knows they acted in ignorance, as their leaders did, but this is how God fulfilled what all the prophets had said, that his Messiah would suffer. So they must repent and turn to God, so that their sins may be wiped out, times of refreshing may come from the Lord, and he may send the Messiah appointed for them, Jesus. Heaven must receive him until the time comes for God to restore everything, as he promised long ago through the prophets. Moses said God would raise up a prophet like him, whom they must listen to in everything, and anyone who will not listen will be cut off. All the prophets from Samuel on foretold these days. They are heirs of the prophets and of the covenant God made with Abraham, when he said that through Abraham’s offspring all peoples on earth would be blessed. God raised up his servant and sent him first to them, to bless them by turning each of them from their wicked ways.
verseByVerse.theology:
Jesus as the Fulfilment of the Covenant with Abraham

Peter closes on the promise to Abraham — in your offspring shall all the families of the earth be blessed (v. 25; cf. Genesis 22:18; 28:14) — and it matters a great deal where that promise was sworn. It is repeated on the mountain, after the knife is stopped and the ram is found caught in the thicket: the promise that the whole world would be blessed through Abraham's line is given at the exact moment God provides a substitute for a beloved son. Peter quotes it in a sermon about a beloved Son for whom no substitute was provided. The gospel, on this reading, is not the abandonment of God's promises to Israel but their arrival — not a second plan drawn up after the first failed, but the first plan reaching the date it had been set for. Reformed biblical theology insists that the covenant of grace runs unbroken from Genesis to Revelation and finds its definitive form in Christ, which is why Peter can preach this to Jews in the temple courts without once suggesting that they should change religion.
verseByVerse.examples: Then: Peter preached to people who bore the most direct responsibility there was — you denied the Holy and Righteous One — and then called them brothers three verses later and told them the blessing was coming to them first. Now: The order has never changed. A gospel that cannot name what a man has actually done has nothing to forgive him for; a gospel that names it and leaves him standing there is not the gospel at all. Peter does both in one sermon, and the second half is longer than the first.

verseByVerse.quote: While he clung to Peter and John, all the people, utterly astounded, ran together to them in the portico called Solomon's. And when Peter saw it he addressed the people: "Men of Israel, why do you wonder at this, or why do you stare at us, as though by our own power or piety we have made him walk?"
verseByVerse.commentary:
While the man held on to Peter and John, all the people were astonished and came running to them in the place called Solomon’s Colonnade. When Peter saw this, he said to them: “Fellow Israelites, why does this surprise you? Why do you stare at us as if by our own power or godliness we had made this man walk?”

Solomon’s Portico. A covered colonnade along the eastern side of the temple courts, traditionally thought to date back to Solomon. Jesus taught there (John 10:23), and the early church met there (5:12).

Not our power. Peter immediately deflects attention from himself. Compare Paul and Barnabas at Lystra (14:14–15).

On a Tuesday. When people praise you for something God did, redirect the credit.
verseByVerse.note: Solomon’s portico was a covered colonnade along the east side of the temple courts.

verseByVerse.quote: "The God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, the God of our fathers, glorified his servant Jesus, whom you delivered over and denied in the presence of Pilate, when he had decided to release him."
verseByVerse.commentary:
“The God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the God of our fathers, has glorified his servant Jesus. You handed him over to be killed, and you disowned him before Pilate, though he had decided to let him go.”

The God of the fathers. Peter preaches no new God, but the God of Israel’s patriarchs (Exodus 3:6).

His servant. Pais: servant or child. An echo of Isaiah’s Servant: “Behold, my servant shall act wisely; he shall be high and lifted up, and shall be exalted” (Isaiah 52:13). The same Servant was “pierced for our transgressions” (Isaiah 53:5).

Pilate wanted to release him. Luke 23:4, 14–16, 20, 22. The Roman judge found him innocent three times.

On a Tuesday. Read Isaiah 52:13–53:12 and see how fully it describes Jesus.
verseByVerse.note: “His servant” echoes Isaiah’s Servant, who would be “lifted up” and glorified.

parallels.desc: my servant shall be high and lifted up

verseByVerse.quote: "But you denied the Holy and Righteous One, and asked for a murderer to be granted to you, and you killed the Author of life, whom God raised from the dead. To this we are witnesses."
verseByVerse.commentary:
“You disowned the Holy and Righteous One and asked for a murderer to be released to you. You killed the author of life, but God raised him from the dead. We are witnesses of this.”

The Holy and Righteous One. Titles of the Messiah, emphasising his innocence and purity.

A murderer. Barabbas, a rebel who had committed murder (Luke 23:18–19, “Away with this man, and release to us Barabbas”). They chose a killer and killed the giver of life.

Author of life. Archēgos: founder, pioneer, leader, prince. The one who leads others into life (Hebrews 2:10; 12:2). The irony: they killed the source of life itself.

For worship. Jesus took Barabbas’s place. In a sense, every believer is Barabbas: guilty, set free because the innocent one died.

verseByVerse.quote: "And his name — by faith in his name — has made this man strong whom you see and know, and the faith that is through Jesus has given the man this perfect health in the presence of you all."
verseByVerse.commentary:
“By faith in the name of Jesus, this man whom you see and know was made strong. It is Jesus’ name and the faith that comes through him that has completely healed him, as you can all see.”

Faith in his name. Whose faith? Probably Peter’s, since the man asked only for money. But the faith itself “is through Jesus”: a gift from him.

Perfect health. Holoklēria: wholeness, soundness in every part.

On a Tuesday. Faith is not a force we generate. It is trust in Jesus, and even that he gives.

verseByVerse.quote: "And now, brothers, I know that you acted in ignorance, as did also your rulers. But what God foretold by the mouth of all the prophets, that his Christ would suffer, he thus fulfilled."
verseByVerse.commentary:
“Now, fellow Israelites, I know that you acted in ignorance, as did your leaders. But this is how God fulfilled what he had foretold through all the prophets, saying that his Messiah would suffer.”

In ignorance. They did not know who Jesus really was. As Jesus prayed, “Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do” (Luke 23:34). Paul said the same of himself (1 Timothy 1:13). Ignorance does not remove guilt, but it opens the door to mercy.

A suffering Messiah. Unexpected to most Jews, but foretold (Isaiah 53; Psalm 22; Luke 24:26–27, 46).

On a Tuesday. When someone opposes the gospel, remember they may be acting in ignorance. Pray for them as Jesus did.

verseByVerse.quote: "Repent therefore, and turn back, that your sins may be blotted out,"
verseByVerse.commentary:
“Repent, then, and turn to God, so that your sins may be wiped out.”

Repent and turn. Two words: change your mind, and turn your life around.

Blotted out. Exaleiphthēnai: wiped clean, like writing erased from a wax tablet or a debt cancelled (Colossians 2:14). “I, I am he who blots out your transgressions for my own sake” (Isaiah 43:25).

On a Tuesday. Whatever you have done, God can wipe it out completely. Repent and turn.

parallels.desc: I am he who blots out your transgressions

verseByVerse.quote: "that times of refreshing may come from the presence of the Lord, and that he may send the Christ appointed for you, Jesus, whom heaven must receive until the time for restoring all the things about which God spoke by the mouth of his holy prophets long ago."
verseByVerse.commentary:
“…that times of refreshing may come from the Lord, and that he may send the Messiah, who has been appointed for you, even Jesus. Heaven must receive him until the time comes for God to restore everything, as he promised long ago through his holy prophets.”

Times of refreshing. Relief, renewal, like cool air after heat. Both now (forgiveness and the Spirit) and at Christ’s return.

Heaven must receive him. Christ is bodily in heaven until his return. This is one reason Reformed Christians reject the idea that his body is physically present in the bread of communion (see on 1 Corinthians 10:16).

The restoration of all things. Apokatastasis. What does it mean?

Origen and some later writers used this word for the final restoration of every creature, even the devil, to God (universalism).

Dispensationalists see the restoration of Israel’s kingdom.

Most interpreters see the renewal of creation at Christ’s return: “in the new world” (Matthew 19:28), when “the creation itself will be set free from its bondage to corruption” (Romans 8:21).

Verdict: the third. It is the restoration “that God spoke by the prophets”, the new heavens and new earth (Isaiah 65:17), not the salvation of everyone, for verse 23 warns that those who do not listen will be destroyed.

A textual note. Later manuscripts (followed by the KJV, “Jesus Christ, which before was preached unto you”) read “preached before” instead of “appointed”. The two Greek words are similar; “appointed” is better attested.

For worship. Thank God that he will restore all things. Every broken thing in creation is waiting for that day.

parallels.desc: new heavens and a new earth

verseByVerse.quote: "Moses said, 'The Lord God will raise up for you a prophet like me from your brothers. You shall listen to him in whatever he tells you.'"
verseByVerse.commentary:
“For Moses said, ‘The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people; you must listen to everything he tells you.’”

Deuteronomy 18:15–19. God promised “a prophet like me from among you”. Israel waited for this prophet (John 1:21; 6:14). Peter says it is Jesus.

Like Moses. A deliverer, mediator of a covenant, lawgiver, worker of signs, who spoke with God face to face. Jesus is all these, and more (Hebrews 3:1–6).

Listen to him. At the transfiguration the Father said, “This is my Son, my Chosen One; listen to him!” (Luke 9:35).

On a Tuesday. Are you listening to Jesus? Read one of his sermons this week, slowly.

parallels.desc: a prophet like me from among you

verseByVerse.quote: "And it shall be that every soul who does not listen to that prophet shall be destroyed from the people. And all the prophets who have spoken, from Samuel and those who came after him, also proclaimed these days."
verseByVerse.commentary:
“Anyone who does not listen to him will be completely cut off from their people. Indeed, beginning with Samuel, all the prophets who have spoken have foretold these days.”

Destroyed from the people. Drawing on Deuteronomy 18:19 and Leviticus 23:29. To reject the Messiah is to cut oneself off from God’s people.

Samuel. The prophet who anointed David, the ancestor of the Messiah.

On a Tuesday. Neutrality about Jesus is not possible. Listening to him is life; refusing is loss.

parallels.desc: Nathan’s prophecy in Samuel’s days

verseByVerse.quote: "You are the sons of the prophets and of the covenant that God made with your fathers, saying to Abraham, 'And in your offspring shall all the families of the earth be blessed.' God, having raised up his servant, sent him to you first, to bless you by turning every one of you from your wickedness."
verseByVerse.commentary:
“And you are heirs of the prophets and of the covenant God made with your fathers. He said to Abraham, ‘Through your offspring all peoples on earth will be blessed.’ When God raised up his servant, he sent him first to you to bless you by turning each of you from your wicked ways.”

Sons of the covenant. The Jewish hearers are heirs of God’s promises. The gospel is offered to them first.

Genesis 22:18. “In your offspring shall all the nations of the earth be blessed.” Paul explains that the offspring is Christ (Galatians 3:16).

To you first. “To the Jew first and also to the Greek” (Romans 1:16). Then to all nations.

The blessing. Not wealth or political power, but being turned from wickedness. Salvation from sin is the greatest blessing.

For worship. Thank God that his promise to Abraham reached you, through Christ.

parallels.desc: in you all the families of the earth shall be blessed

3.theology: The Name of Jesus. “His name — by faith in his name — has made this man strong” (v. 16). This verse is not about a formula but about a person. The name in the ancient world carried the authority and presence of the one who bore it. When Peter speaks the name of Jesus, he is not invoking magic; he is acting in the delegated authority of the reigning Christ. The healing is an act of the risen Lord performed through his servant. Faith is the hand that reaches for what the name offers. And what the name offers is the full power of the one who conquered death — resurrection life, flowing through a living faith, into a broken body and a guilty conscience alike.
3.examples:
Then: A man lame from birth, set daily at the gate of the temple he could not enter, excluded by his condition from the presence he longed for. His whole life had been one long reaching-out of an empty hand. And then, in the name of Jesus, he entered the temple walking.

Now: The church still carries what the world cannot give. No program, no therapy, no government initiative can do what the name of Jesus does — not because those things are worthless, but because they cannot raise the dead. The church’s temptation in every generation is to be embarrassed by its true wealth and to offer silver and gold instead. The world has plenty of silver and gold. It has only one name by which it can be saved.

4.title: Boldness Before the Council
4.text: <sup>1</sup>And as they were speaking to the people, the priests and the captain of the temple and the Sadducees came upon them, <sup>2</sup>greatly annoyed because they were teaching the people and proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection from the dead. <sup>3</sup>And they arrested them and put them in custody until the next day, for it was already evening. <sup>4</sup>But many of those who had heard the word believed, and the number of the men came to about five thousand. <sup>5</sup>On the next day their rulers and elders and scribes gathered together in Jerusalem, <sup>6</sup>with Annas the high priest and Caiaphas and John and Alexander, and all who were of the high-priestly family. <sup>7</sup>And when they had set them in the midst, they inquired, “By what power or by what name did you do this?” <sup>8</sup>Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them, “Rulers of the people and elders, <sup>9</sup>if we are being examined today concerning a good deed done to a crippled man, by what means this man has been healed, <sup>10</sup>let it be known to all of you and to all the people of Israel that by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead—by him this man is standing before you well. <sup>11</sup>This Jesus is the stone that was rejected by you, the builders, which has become the cornerstone. <sup>12</sup>And there is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved.” <sup>13</sup>Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were uneducated, common men, they were astonished. And they recognized that they had been with Jesus. <sup>14</sup>But seeing the man who was healed standing beside them, they had nothing to say in opposition. <sup>15</sup>But when they had commanded them to leave the council, they conferred with one another, <sup>16</sup>saying, “What shall we do with these men? For that a notable sign has been performed through them is evident to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and we cannot deny it. <sup>17</sup>But in order that it may spread no further among the people, let us warn them to speak no more to anyone in this name.” <sup>18</sup>So they called them and charged them not to speak or teach at all in the name of Jesus. <sup>19</sup>But Peter and John answered them, “Whether it is right in the sight of God to listen to you rather than to God, you must judge, <sup>20</sup>for we cannot but speak of what we have seen and heard.” <sup>21</sup>And when they had further threatened them, they let them go, finding no way to punish them, because of the people, for all were praising God for what had happened. <sup>22</sup>For the man on whom this sign of healing was performed was more than forty years old. <sup>23</sup>When they were released, they went to their friends and reported what the chief priests and the elders had said to them. <sup>24</sup>And when they heard it, they lifted their voices together to God and said, “Sovereign Lord, who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and everything in them, <sup>25</sup>who through the mouth of our father David, your servant, said by the Holy Spirit, ‘Why did the Gentiles rage, and the peoples plot in vain? <sup>26</sup>The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers were gathered together, against the Lord and against his Anointed’— <sup>27</sup>for truly in this city there were gathered together against your holy servant Jesus, whom you anointed, both Herod and Pontius Pilate, along with the Gentiles and the peoples of Israel, <sup>28</sup>to do whatever your hand and your plan had predestined to take place. <sup>29</sup>And now, Lord, look upon their threats and grant to your servants to continue to speak your word with all boldness, <sup>30</sup>while you stretch out your hand to heal, and signs and wonders are performed through the name of your holy servant Jesus.” <sup>31</sup>And when they had prayed, the place in which they were gathered together was shaken, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and continued to speak the word of God with boldness. <sup>32</sup>Now the full number of those who believed were of one heart and soul, and no one said that any of the things that belonged to him was his own, but they had everything in common. <sup>33</sup>And with great power the apostles were giving their testimony to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus, and great grace was upon them all. <sup>34</sup>There was not a needy person among them, for as many as were owners of lands or houses sold them and brought the proceeds of what was sold <sup>35</sup>and laid it at the apostles’ feet, and it was distributed to each as any had need. <sup>36</sup>Thus Joseph, who was also called by the apostles Barnabas (which means son of encouragement), a Levite, a native of Cyprus, <sup>37</sup>sold a field that belonged to him and brought the money and laid it at the apostles’ feet.
4.overview:
The healing and Peter’s sermon bring the first persecution. The temple authorities were dominated by the Sadducees, the priestly aristocracy who controlled the temple, cooperated with Rome to keep order, and denied the resurrection of the dead. Two Galileans proclaiming in the temple courts that Jesus had been raised were a threat on every count. Peter and John are arrested and brought before the Sanhedrin, the Jewish ruling council, with the former high priest Annas, his son-in-law Caiaphas and the high priestly family, the very men who had condemned Jesus weeks earlier. Filled with the Spirit, Peter tells them the man was healed by the name of Jesus, the stone they rejected who has become the cornerstone, and that there is salvation in no other name.

The council is astonished at the boldness of these untrained men, recognises that they had been with Jesus, and cannot deny the miracle, so it orders them to stop speaking in his name. Peter and John reply that they must obey God and cannot stop speaking of what they have seen and heard. Released, they return to the believers, who pray using Psalm 2: the nations and rulers raged against the Lord’s Anointed, just as Herod and Pilate, the Gentiles and Israel had done, but only to carry out what God had planned. They do not ask for safety but for boldness and for God to stretch out his hand to heal. The place shakes, they are filled with the Spirit and speak boldly. The chapter ends with the church’s generosity: no one in need, owners selling property for the poor, and a Levite from Cyprus, Joseph, nicknamed Barnabas, “son of encouragement”, selling a field and laying the money at the apostles’ feet.

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: While Peter and John were speaking to the people, the priests, the captain of the temple guard and the Sadducees came up, greatly disturbed that the apostles were teaching the people and proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection of the dead. They seized them and, since it was evening, put them in jail until the next day. But many who heard the message believed, and the number of men grew to about five thousand. The next day the rulers, elders and teachers of the law met in Jerusalem, with Annas the high priest, Caiaphas, John, Alexander and others of the high priest’s family. They had Peter and John brought before them and asked by what power or name they had done this. Filled with the Spirit, Peter replied that if they were being questioned about an act of kindness to a disabled man, everyone in Israel should know it was by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom they crucified and God raised, that this man stood there healed. Jesus is the stone the builders rejected, now the cornerstone, and salvation is found in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven by which people must be saved. Seeing the courage of Peter and John and realising they were ordinary men with no formal training, the council was astonished and recognised that they had been with Jesus. With the healed man standing there, they had nothing to say. They sent them out, conferred, and admitted that an undeniable miracle had happened which everyone in Jerusalem knew about. To stop it spreading, they warned the apostles not to speak or teach in Jesus’ name. Peter and John answered that the council must judge whether it is right before God to obey them rather than God; as for themselves, they could not help speaking about what they had seen and heard. After further threats the council let them go, because they could find no way to punish them without upsetting the people, who were all praising God for the healing of a man over forty years old.
verseByVerse.theology:
The Exclusivity of Christ

Peter's declaration in v. 12 — there is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved — is among the clearest statements of Christ's exclusive lordship in salvation anywhere in Scripture, and it is worth noticing that it is spoken in a courtroom, to men who could imprison him for it. Reformed theology has always held this exclusivity to follow from the incarnation itself: if God became flesh in one particular person, in one particular place, at one particular hour of history, then salvation is tied to that person and cannot be detached from him. A plurality of saviours would require a plurality of incarnations, which is not a thing the gospel can be stretched to accommodate. And the same logic that makes the claim exclusive makes it universal: the name is given among men, offered, held out — the door is single and it is not shut.
verseByVerse.examples: Then: Peter and John were laymen without rabbinic training, standing in the middle of the supreme court of Israel, and their boldness astonished the men trying them — parresia, a word that in Greek public life meant the free speech of a citizen in the assembly, the very thing a slave did not have. Now: The same Spirit who supplied it is given to every believer, and the church prays for more of it in this very chapter (v. 29). Boldness in the New Testament is not a temperament. It is a gift, asked for and granted, and it is perfectly compatible with being frightened.

verseByVerse.quote: And as they were speaking to the people, the priests and the captain of the temple and the Sadducees came upon them, greatly annoyed because they were teaching the people and proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection from the dead.
verseByVerse.commentary:
While Peter and John were speaking to the people, the priests, the captain of the temple guard and the Sadducees came up to them. They were greatly disturbed because the apostles were teaching the people, proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection of the dead.

The captain of the temple. The commander of the temple police, a priest second in rank to the high priest.

The Sadducees. The aristocratic priestly party. They accepted only the five books of Moses as fully authoritative, denied the resurrection, angels and spirits (23:8), and worked with Rome to keep order and their own power.

Annoyed. For three reasons: unauthorised laymen were teaching in the temple; they were preaching resurrection, which the Sadducees denied; and they were proclaiming the man the Sadducees had helped to crucify.

On a Tuesday. The gospel will disturb some people, especially those whose power or beliefs it threatens. Do not be surprised.
verseByVerse.note: The captain of the temple commanded the temple police and ranked next to the high priest. The Sadducees, the priestly party, denied the resurrection.

verseByVerse.quote: And they arrested them and put them in custody until the next day, for it was already evening. But many of those who had heard the word believed, and the number of the men came to about five thousand.
verseByVerse.commentary:
They seized Peter and John and, because it was evening, put them in jail until the next day. But many who heard the message believed; so the number of men who believed grew to about five thousand.

Custody. Hearings were not normally held at night.

But many believed. The arrest did not stop the growth. Luke repeatedly sets persecution and growth side by side.

Five thousand men. Andrōn: men specifically, perhaps heads of households. With women and children the church may have been much larger.

On a Tuesday. Opposition cannot stop God’s word. Christians in China, Iran and elsewhere have seen the church grow under persecution.
verseByVerse.note: Hearings were not normally held at night.

verseByVerse.quote: On the next day their rulers and elders and scribes gathered together in Jerusalem, with Annas the high priest and Caiaphas and John and Alexander, and all who were of the high-priestly family.
verseByVerse.commentary:
The next day the rulers, the elders and the teachers of the law met in Jerusalem. Annas the high priest was there, and so were Caiaphas, John, Alexander and others of the high priest’s family.

The Sanhedrin. The supreme Jewish council of seventy-one members, chaired by the high priest, made up of chief priests, elders (leading laymen) and scribes (experts in the law). They sat in a semicircle.

Annas. High priest from AD 6 to 15, deposed by the Romans but still regarded as the real power. Five of his sons and his son-in-law became high priest after him. Jesus was taken to him first (John 18:13).

Caiaphas. Annas’s son-in-law, high priest AD 18–36, who had said it was better that one man die for the people (John 11:49–50). A bone box (ossuary) inscribed “Joseph son of Caiaphas” was found in Jerusalem in 1990.

The same men. The council that condemned Jesus now faces his apostles.

On a Tuesday. The apostles stood before the most powerful men in their nation. God gives courage for the moment.
verseByVerse.note: The rulers, elders and scribes made up the Sanhedrin. Annas had been high priest earlier and remained head of the family; Caiaphas was the serving high priest.

verseByVerse.quote: And when they had set them in the midst, they inquired, "By what power or by what name did you do this?"
verseByVerse.commentary:
They had Peter and John brought before them and began to question them: “By what power or what name did you do this?”

By what name? In the ancient world, healers often invoked the name of a god or a spirit. The council suspected sorcery or a rival authority.

On a Tuesday. When people ask how something good happened in your life, it is an opening to name Jesus.

parallels.desc: by what authority?

verseByVerse.quote: Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them, "Rulers of the people and elders, if we are being examined today concerning a good deed done to a crippled man, by what means this man has been healed,"
verseByVerse.commentary:
Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them: “Rulers and elders of the people! If we are being called to account today for an act of kindness shown to a man who was lame, and are being asked how he was healed…”

Filled with the Spirit. A fresh filling for a particular task, as Jesus promised: “do not be anxious how you are to speak or what you are to say, for what you are to say will be given to you in that hour” (Matthew 10:19).

A good deed. Peter points out the absurdity: they are on trial for helping a disabled man.

On a Tuesday. If you are criticised for doing good in Christ’s name, answer calmly, and trust the Spirit.

parallels.desc: I will give you a mouth and wisdom

verseByVerse.quote: "let it be known to all of you and to all the people of Israel that by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead — by him this man is standing before you well. This Jesus is the stone that was rejected by you, the builders, which has become the cornerstone."
verseByVerse.commentary:
“…then know this, you and all the people of Israel: it is by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified but whom God raised from the dead, that this man stands before you healed. Jesus is ‘the stone you builders rejected, which has become the cornerstone.’”

You crucified, God raised. The apostolic message in a sentence.

Psalm 118:22. “The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.” Jesus applied it to himself (Luke 20:17). The builders are the nation’s leaders, the very men Peter is addressing. The cornerstone, laid first, set the line of the whole building.

On a Tuesday. What the world rejects, God may make the foundation. Do not measure worth by human approval.

parallels.desc: the stone the builders rejected

verseByVerse.quote: "And there is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved."
verseByVerse.commentary:
“Salvation is found in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given to mankind by which we must be saved.”

No other name. One of the clearest statements of the uniqueness of Christ. Jesus: “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me” (John 14:6). “There is one God, and there is one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus” (1 Timothy 2:5).

Must. A divine necessity. Not one way among many.

Can people be saved without knowing Christ?

Pluralism (John Hick): all religions are valid paths to God.

Inclusivism (Karl Rahner’s “anonymous Christians”, Clark Pinnock): salvation is only through Christ, but some may be saved by him without knowing him, through responding to the light they have.

Exclusivism, or particularism: salvation is through conscious faith in Christ.

Verdict: exclusivism. Peter spoke to devout Jews who worshipped the true God, and told them they too needed the name of Jesus. Paul asks, “how are they to hear without someone preaching?” (Romans 10:14). This should drive us to mission, not to arrogance. The Judge of all the earth will do right (Genesis 18:25) with those who never heard; our task is to tell them.

On a Tuesday. If Jesus is the only way, then telling your friends about him is the most loving thing you can do.

verseByVerse.quote: Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were uneducated, common men, they were astonished. And they recognized that they had been with Jesus. But seeing the man who was healed standing beside them, they had nothing to say in opposition.
verseByVerse.commentary:
When they saw the courage of Peter and John and realised that they were unschooled, ordinary men, they were astonished, and they took note that these men had been with Jesus.

Boldness. Parrēsia: freedom of speech, confidence. A key word in Acts (4:29, 31; 28:31).

Uneducated, common. Agrammatoi and idiōtai: not illiterate, but without formal rabbinic training, laymen. The same was said of Jesus (John 7:15).

They had been with Jesus. Their boldness reminded the council of him. The best training for witness is time with Jesus.

On a Tuesday. You do not need a theology degree to speak about Christ. You need to be with him.
verseByVerse.note: “Uneducated, common men” means they had no formal training in the law under a rabbi — not that they were illiterate.

verseByVerse.quote: But when they had commanded them to leave the council, they conferred with one another, saying, "What shall we do with these men? For that a notable sign has been performed through them is evident to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and we cannot deny it."
verseByVerse.commentary:
But since they could see the man who had been healed standing there with them, there was nothing they could say. So they ordered them to withdraw from the Sanhedrin and then conferred together. “What are we going to do with these men?” they asked. “Everyone living in Jerusalem knows they have performed a notable sign, and we cannot deny it.”

The healed man. The best argument stood in the room.

We cannot deny it. The council admitted the miracle but refused its meaning. Evidence alone does not convert a hardened heart (Luke 16:31).

How did Luke know? Perhaps from a member of the council who later believed, such as Nicodemus, or from priests who became disciples (6:7), or from Paul, who was a Pharisee in Jerusalem.

On a Tuesday. Some people will not believe whatever evidence you give. Keep praying for them.

verseByVerse.quote: "But in order that it may spread no further among the people, let us warn them to speak no more to anyone in this name." So they called them and charged them not to speak or teach at all in the name of Jesus.
verseByVerse.commentary:
“But to stop this thing from spreading any further among the people, we must warn them to speak no longer to anyone in this name.”

Containment. Their concern was not truth but control.

In this name. They will not even say “Jesus”.

On a Tuesday. In many workplaces, Christians are told they may be religious privately, but not speak of Jesus. Think through how you will respond.

verseByVerse.quote: But Peter and John answered them, "Whether it is right in the sight of God to listen to you rather than to God, you must judge, for we cannot but speak of what we have seen and heard."
verseByVerse.commentary:
But Peter and John replied, “Which is right in God’s eyes: to listen to you, or to him? You be the judges! As for us, we cannot help speaking about what we have seen and heard.”

God or men. The foundation of Christian civil disobedience. Compare the Hebrew midwives, who “feared God and did not do as the king of Egypt commanded them” (Exodus 1:17), and Daniel’s friends: “we will not serve your gods” (Daniel 3:18).

When should Christians disobey authorities? Christians are commanded to obey governing authorities: “Let every person be subject to the governing authorities” (Romans 13:1). But when authorities command what God forbids, or forbid what God commands, God must be obeyed. The Reformed tradition (Calvin, Knox, Rutherford) developed this into a careful theory of resistance through lawful lesser authorities. Verdict: disobey only when obedience would mean sin; do so openly and peacefully; and accept the consequences, as the apostles did (5:41). This is not a licence to ignore laws we dislike.

We cannot but speak. Witnesses must testify.

On a Tuesday. If you are told to lie, cover up wrongdoing or deny Christ at work, you must obey God. Be respectful, honest and prepared to pay a cost.

parallels.desc: we must obey God rather than men

verseByVerse.quote: And when they had further threatened them, they let them go, finding no way to punish them, because of the people, for all were praising God for what had happened. For the man on whom this sign of healing was performed was more than forty years old.
verseByVerse.commentary:
After further threats they let them go. They could not decide how to punish them, because all the people were praising God for what had happened. For the man who was miraculously healed was over forty years old.

The people. Public opinion protected the apostles for now.

Over forty. Luke the doctor adds a medical detail: a lifelong condition, impossible to fake.

For worship. The whole city praised God. Pray that God will do things in your town that make people praise him.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 23–37 — Prayer, Power, and the Community of Grace
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Released, Peter and John went back to their own people and reported what the chief priests and elders had said. Hearing it, the believers prayed together to the sovereign Lord, maker of heaven, earth, sea and everything in them. They recalled that the Holy Spirit had spoken through David, asking why the nations rage and the peoples plot in vain, why kings and rulers band together against the Lord and his Anointed. That is what had happened in Jerusalem: Herod and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles and the people of Israel, conspired against God’s holy servant Jesus, whom he anointed, doing only what God’s power and will had decided beforehand. Now they asked the Lord to consider the threats, and to enable his servants to speak his word with great boldness while he stretched out his hand to heal and perform signs and wonders through the name of his holy servant Jesus. When they had prayed, the place where they met was shaken, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke God’s word boldly. All the believers were one in heart and mind. No one claimed their possessions as their own; they shared everything. With great power the apostles continued to testify to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus, and great grace was on them all. There was no one needy among them, because from time to time owners of land or houses sold them and brought the money to the apostles, who distributed it to anyone in need. Joseph, a Levite from Cyprus whom the apostles called Barnabas, meaning son of encouragement, sold a field he owned and laid the money at the apostles’ feet.
verseByVerse.theology:
The Sovereignty of God and Human Responsibility

Verses 27 and 28 are among the most explicit statements of divine sovereignty in the New Testament: Herod, Pontius Pilate, the Gentiles and the peoples of Israel gathered against Jesus to do whatever your hand and your plan had predestined to take place. What is striking is the setting. This is not a chapter of argument. It is a prayer, offered by frightened people the morning after a night in custody. The doctrine is not being defended here; it is being leaned on. Reformed theology has always insisted that the two truths — real human guilt and a real divine purpose — must be held together rather than traded against each other, and this chapter shows what holding them together is actually for. If the murder of the Son of God fell inside the plan, then a threat delivered that morning falls inside it too. Which is why the prayer runs straight on from verse 28 to verse 29 without a pause. The sovereignty is not the conclusion of the prayer. It is the ground they are standing on in order to ask for courage.
verseByVerse.examples: Then: Luke reports the result of the church's generosity in a sentence that echoes the law of Moses: there was not a needy person among them (compare Deuteronomy 15:4). Deuteronomy had held exactly that out as a possibility, attached a condition Israel never met, and admitted in the same chapter that the poor would never cease out of the land. What fifteen centuries of covenant history had not produced, the Spirit produced in Jerusalem inside a year. Now: The particular form belonged to a moment; the open hand does not. And Luke's arrangement is worth attention — he sets the giving immediately beside the preaching, in the same paragraph, so that the community's life and the apostles' message are not two subjects but one.

verseByVerse.quote: When they were released, they went to their friends and reported what the chief priests and the elders had said to them. And when they heard it, they lifted their voices together to God and said, "Sovereign Lord, who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and everything in them,"
verseByVerse.commentary:
On their release, Peter and John went back to their own people and reported all that the chief priests and the elders had said to them. When they heard this, they raised their voices together in prayer to God. “Sovereign Lord,” they said, “you made the heavens and the earth and the sea, and everything in them.”

Their friends. The church: their true family.

Together. Homothymadon, with one mind.

Sovereign Lord. Despota: absolute master, the word a slave used for his owner. They begin not with their problem but with God’s greatness as Creator. If he made everything, the Sanhedrin is small.

On a Tuesday. When trouble comes, begin your prayer with who God is before you tell him what you need.

parallels.desc: who made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them

verseByVerse.quote: "who through the mouth of our father David, your servant, said by the Holy Spirit, 'Why did the Gentiles rage, and the peoples plot in vain? The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers were gathered together, against the Lord and against his Anointed' —"
verseByVerse.commentary:
“You spoke by the Holy Spirit through the mouth of your servant, our father David: ‘Why do the nations rage and the peoples plot in vain? The kings of the earth rise up and the rulers band together against the Lord and against his anointed one.’”

Psalm 2. A royal psalm: the nations rebel against God and his anointed King, but God laughs and installs his King on Zion. The early Christians saw it fulfilled in the opposition to Jesus.

A textual note. The Greek of this verse is unusually awkward in the best manuscripts (“through the mouth of our father David your servant, by the Holy Spirit”), which may reflect a very early copying slip. Later manuscripts, followed by the KJV (“Who by the mouth of thy servant David hast said”), smoothed it. The meaning is clear: God spoke by the Spirit through David.

On a Tuesday. Use the Psalms in your own prayers, as the early church did.

parallels.desc: why do the nations rage?

verseByVerse.quote: "for truly in this city there were gathered together against your holy servant Jesus, whom you anointed, both Herod and Pontius Pilate, along with the Gentiles and the peoples of Israel, to do whatever your hand and your plan had predestined to take place."
verseByVerse.commentary:
“Indeed Herod and Pontius Pilate met together with the Gentiles and the people of Israel in this city to conspire against your holy servant Jesus, whom you anointed. They did what your power and will had decided beforehand should happen.”

Herod and Pilate. Herod Antipas, ruler of Galilee, and the Roman governor. Enemies before, they became friends on the day Jesus was condemned (Luke 23:12).

Predestined. Proōrisen. The cross was God’s plan from the beginning. Even the greatest evil was under God’s sovereign hand, though the people who did it were guilty (2:23).

Comfort in persecution. If the cross was in God’s plan, so are the threats against the apostles. Nothing is outside his control.

On a Tuesday. When evil things happen to you, God has not lost control. He can use even this for good (Genesis 50:20; Romans 8:28).
verseByVerse.note: Herod is Herod Antipas.

verseByVerse.quote: "And now, Lord, look upon their threats and grant to your servants to continue to speak your word with all boldness, while you stretch out your hand to heal, and signs and wonders are performed through the name of your holy servant Jesus."
verseByVerse.commentary:
“Now, Lord, consider their threats and enable your servants to speak your word with great boldness. Stretch out your hand to heal and perform signs and wonders through the name of your holy servant Jesus.”

They did not ask for safety. They did not pray for the threats to stop, or for the council to be punished, but for boldness to keep speaking.

Your servants. Douloi: slaves of the Sovereign Master.

Signs and wonders. To confirm the word, as the Lord had done (Mark 16:20; Hebrews 2:4).

On a Tuesday. Next time you face opposition for your faith, pray this prayer: not “make it go away”, but “give me courage to keep speaking”.

parallels.desc: pray that words may be given me to open my mouth boldly

verseByVerse.quote: And when they had prayed, the place in which they were gathered together was shaken, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and continued to speak the word of God with boldness.
verseByVerse.commentary:
After they prayed, the place where they were meeting was shaken. And they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke the word of God boldly.

Shaken. A sign of God’s presence, as at Sinai (Exodus 19:18) and in Isaiah’s vision (Isaiah 6:4).

Filled again. The same people filled at Pentecost (2:4) are filled again. The Spirit’s filling is not a once-for-all event but repeated as needed (Ephesians 5:18, literally “keep on being filled”).

The answer. Exactly what they asked for: boldness.

On a Tuesday. Ask God to fill you with his Spirit today, for whatever you face.

parallels.desc: the whole mountain trembled

verseByVerse.quote: Now the full number of those who believed were of one heart and soul, and no one said that any of the things that belonged to him was his own, but they had everything in common. And with great power the apostles were giving their testimony to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus, and great grace was upon them all.
verseByVerse.commentary:
All the believers were one in heart and mind. No one claimed that any of their possessions was their own, but they shared everything they had. With great power the apostles continued to testify to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus. And God’s grace was so powerfully at work in them all.

One heart and soul. A Greek ideal of friendship (Aristotle said friends are “one soul in two bodies”). The church lived it.

Not their own. Not that they abolished ownership, but that they did not cling to it.

The resurrection. The centre of the apostles’ witness.

Great grace. God’s favour visibly on them.

On a Tuesday. What do you regard as “mine”? Offer one thing this week for someone else’s use.

verseByVerse.quote: There was not a needy person among them, for as many as were owners of lands or houses sold them and brought the proceeds of what was sold and laid it at the apostles' feet, and it was distributed to each as any had need.
verseByVerse.commentary:
There were no needy persons among them. For from time to time those who owned land or houses sold them, brought the money from the sales and put it at the apostles’ feet, and it was distributed to anyone who had need.

No needy person. Echoing Deuteronomy 15:4: “there will be no poor among you”. The church fulfilled the ideal Israel had failed to keep.

From time to time. The Greek tense suggests repeated, occasional sales as needs arose, not a single act of pooling everything.

At the apostles’ feet. A gesture of placing something under another’s authority. The apostles managed the fund (until 6:1–6).

On a Tuesday. Does your church have a fund for members in need? Give to it, and use it wisely.
verseByVerse.note: Laying gifts at someone’s feet placed them under his authority.

parallels.desc: there will be no poor among you

verseByVerse.quote: Thus Joseph, who was also called by the apostles Barnabas (which means son of encouragement), a Levite, a native of Cyprus, sold a field that belonged to him and brought the money and laid it at the apostles' feet.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Joseph, a Levite from Cyprus, whom the apostles called Barnabas (which means “son of encouragement”), sold a field he owned and brought the money and put it at the apostles’ feet.

Barnabas. One of the great figures of Acts. “Son of” is a Semitic way of saying “characterised by”. He lived up to his name: he welcomed the converted Saul when others were afraid (9:27), encouraged the new Gentile church at Antioch (11:22–26), and gave Mark a second chance (15:37–39).

A Levite. Levites originally had no land inheritance in Israel (Numbers 18:20), but by this time some owned property.

Cyprus. A large island in the eastern Mediterranean with a big Jewish community. Barnabas later took the gospel there (13:4).

A model. His gift sets up the contrast with Ananias and Sapphira in the next chapter.

For worship. Thank God for the Barnabases in your life. Then be one: encourage someone today.
verseByVerse.note: Cyprus was a large island in the eastern Mediterranean with a big Jewish community.

4.theology: The Sovereignty of God and Mission. The prayer of Acts 4:24–30 is a theology lecture compressed into seven verses. God is addressed as despotēs — Sovereign Lord, absolute Master — who made heaven and earth and everything in them. Herod and Pilate and the nations, in their opposition to Christ, did “whatever your hand and your plan had predestined to take place.” This is not fatalism; it is the Reformed doctrine of providence applied to history’s darkest moment. And the implication for mission is not paralysis but boldness: if God was sovereign over the crucifixion, he is sovereign over every threat to the gospel. The church does not need favourable conditions to advance the kingdom. It needs the Spirit and the Word. God provides both.
4.examples:
Then: A church only weeks old, under arrest, before the same council that crucified their Lord, with no legal protection, no political allies, no plan B — and they prayed for boldness and were given it. The shaking of the place was God’s receipt: prayer received, boldness granted.

Now: The church in every hostile culture faces the same fork: silence or speech, safety or boldness. The prayer of Acts 4 is still available. The God who shook that room has not grown quiet. He is still the Sovereign Lord who made heaven and earth. And he still grants boldness to those who ask for it — not because they deserve it, but because his Word must go out.

5.title: The Fear of the Lord
5.text: <sup>1</sup>But a man named Ananias, with his wife Sapphira, sold a piece of property, <sup>2</sup>and with his wife’s knowledge he kept back for himself some of the proceeds and brought only a part of it and laid it at the apostles’ feet. <sup>3</sup>But Peter said, “Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit and to keep back for yourself part of the proceeds of the land? <sup>4</sup>While it remained unsold, did it not remain your own? And after it was sold, was it not at your disposal? Why is it that you have contrived this deed in your heart? You have not lied to man but to God.” <sup>5</sup>When Ananias heard these words, he fell down and breathed his last. And great fear came upon all who heard of it. <sup>6</sup>The young men rose and wrapped him up and carried him out and buried him. <sup>7</sup>After an interval of about three hours his wife came in, not knowing what had happened. <sup>8</sup>And Peter said to her, “Tell me whether you sold the land for so much.” And she said, “Yes, for so much.” <sup>9</sup>But Peter said to her, “How is it that you have agreed together to test the Spirit of the Lord? Behold, the feet of those who have buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out.” <sup>10</sup>Immediately she fell down at his feet and breathed her last. When the young men came in they found her dead, and they carried her out and buried her beside her husband. <sup>11</sup>And great fear came upon the whole church and upon all who heard of these things. <sup>12</sup>Now many signs and wonders were regularly done among the people by the hands of the apostles. And they were all together in Solomon’s Portico. <sup>13</sup>None of the rest dared join them, but the people held them in high esteem. <sup>14</sup>And more than ever believers were added to the Lord, multitudes of both men and women, <sup>15</sup>so that they even carried out the sick into the streets and laid them on cots and mats, that as Peter came by at least his shadow might fall on some of them. <sup>16</sup>The people also gathered from the towns around Jerusalem, bringing the sick and those afflicted with unclean spirits, and they were all healed. <sup>17</sup>But the high priest rose up, and all who were with him (that is, the party of the Sadducees), and filled with jealousy <sup>18</sup>they arrested the apostles and put them in the public prison. <sup>19</sup>But during the night an angel of the Lord opened the prison doors and brought them out, and said, <sup>20</sup>“Go and stand in the temple and speak to the people all the words of this Life.” <sup>21</sup>And when they heard this, they entered the temple at daybreak and began to teach. Now when the high priest came, and those who were with him, they called together the council, all the senate of the people of Israel and sent to the prison to have them brought. <sup>22</sup>But when the officers came, they did not find them in the prison, so they returned and reported, <sup>23</sup>“We found the prison securely locked and the guards standing at the doors, but when we opened them we found no one inside.” <sup>24</sup>Now when the captain of the temple and the chief priests heard these words, they were greatly perplexed about them, wondering what this would come to. <sup>25</sup>And someone came and told them, “Look! The men whom you put in prison are standing in the temple and teaching the people.” <sup>26</sup>Then the captain with the officers went and brought them, but not by force, for they were afraid of being stoned by the people. <sup>27</sup>And when they had brought them, they set them before the council. And the high priest questioned them, <sup>28</sup>saying, “We strictly charged you not to teach in this name, yet here you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching, and you intend to bring this man’s blood upon us.” <sup>29</sup>But Peter and the apostles answered, “We must obey God rather than men. <sup>30</sup>The God of our fathers raised Jesus, whom you killed by hanging him on a tree. <sup>31</sup>God exalted him at his right hand as Leader and Savior, to give repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins. <sup>32</sup>And we are witnesses to these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey him.” <sup>33</sup>When they heard this, they were enraged and wanted to kill them. <sup>34</sup>But a Pharisee in the council named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law held in honor by all the people, stood up and gave orders to put the men outside for a little while. <sup>35</sup>And he said to them, “Men of Israel, take care what you are about to do with these men. <sup>36</sup>For before these days Theudas rose up, claiming to be somebody, and a number of men, about four hundred, joined him. He was killed, and all who followed him were dispersed and came to nothing. <sup>37</sup>After him Judas the Galilean rose up in the days of the census and drew away some of the people after him. He too perished, and all who followed him were scattered. <sup>38</sup>So in the present case I tell you, keep away from these men and let them alone, for if this plan or this undertaking is of man, it will fail; <sup>39</sup>but if it is of God, you will not be able to overthrow them. You might even be found opposing God!” So they took his advice, <sup>40</sup>and when they had called in the apostles, they beat them and charged them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and let them go. <sup>41</sup>Then they left the presence of the council, rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer dishonor for the name. <sup>42</sup>And every day, in the temple and from house to house, they did not cease teaching and preaching that the Christ is Jesus.
5.overview:
After the bright picture of Barnabas comes a dark one. Ananias and his wife Sapphira sell property and give part of the price while pretending it is the whole, wanting the reputation of generosity without the cost. Peter tells Ananias he has lied not to men but to God, and Ananias falls dead; three hours later Sapphira repeats the lie and dies too. Great fear seizes the whole church, the first time Luke uses that word for the believers. The story echoes Achan, who secretly kept back plunder when Israel entered the promised land (Joshua 7): at the start of a new work of God, sin in the camp is judged severely.

Meanwhile the apostles perform many signs, the sick are carried into the streets in the hope that even Peter’s shadow will fall on them, and multitudes of men and women believe. Jealous, the high priest has the apostles jailed, but an angel opens the doors at night and tells them to go and preach in the temple. Brought before the council again, they answer, “We must obey God rather than men,” and proclaim the risen Jesus as Leader and Saviour. The council wants to kill them, but Gamaliel, the most respected Pharisee teacher of the day, advises caution: movements of human origin fail, as those of Theudas and Judas the Galilean did, but if this is from God they cannot stop it and may find themselves fighting God. The apostles are flogged and released, and leave rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for the Name, and they keep teaching every day that Jesus is the Christ.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 1–16 — Holiness and Power in the Young Church
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: A man named Ananias and his wife Sapphira also sold a piece of property, but with her full knowledge he kept back part of the money and brought the rest to the apostles as if it were the whole. Peter asked him how he had let Satan fill his heart so that he lied to the Holy Spirit and kept back part of the price. The land was his to keep, and after selling it the money was at his disposal. Why had he thought of doing such a thing? He had lied not to people but to God. When Ananias heard this he fell down and died, and great fear came on everyone who heard. The young men wrapped his body, carried him out and buried him. About three hours later his wife came in, not knowing what had happened. Peter asked whether this was the price they got for the land, and she said yes. Peter asked how they could agree to test the Spirit of the Lord, and told her that the men who had buried her husband were at the door and would carry her out too. At once she fell down at his feet and died. The young men came in, found her dead, and buried her beside her husband. Great fear seized the whole church and all who heard. The apostles performed many signs and wonders among the people, and the believers all used to meet together in Solomon’s Colonnade. No one else dared join them, though the people held them in high regard. Yet more and more men and women believed in the Lord and were added to their number. People even brought the sick into the streets on beds and mats so that at least Peter’s shadow might fall on some as he passed. Crowds came from the towns around Jerusalem, bringing the sick and those troubled by impure spirits, and all of them were healed.
verseByVerse.theology:
The Holiness of God and the Danger of Hypocrisy

The deaths of Ananias and Sapphira stand in a recognisable biblical pattern: when God inaugurates something holy, the first sin against it is judged with startling swiftness. Nadab and Abihu at the dawn of the priesthood (Leviticus 10), Achan at Israel's entry into the land (Joshua 7), Uzzah as the ark comes home (2 Samuel 6), and here the first hypocrisy at the birth of the church. These are representative judgements — one public sample of what all sin deserves, set down once. They are not the rule; God's ordinary way is the patient kindness meant to lead to repentance (Romans 2:4), which is precisely why the rest of us are still breathing. A God who never enforced his own holiness would not be holy, and the gospel does not lower that holiness but satisfies it, so that those in Christ may come near to the Holy One with confidence. The second half of the section shows what such a God does with a church that has learned to tremble before him: he fills it, and multiplies it, and heals through it in the open street.
verseByVerse.examples:
Then: A church only weeks old discovered that the Spirit who filled it also searched it — and that the same fear which drove off the hangers-on drew in multitudes.

Now: The pattern repeats wherever religious performance stands in for reality: the testimony allowed to run better than the facts, the prayer that warms when others are listening, the struggle described in the past tense because the present tense would cost too much. Two cautions belong with it. This chapter is not a lever for extracting money — Peter says the field and the proceeds were theirs. And the fear here came from what God did, not from what the leaders did; a congregation frightened of its elders has reproduced what this chapter killed, not what it created. The fear of God makes people honest. The fear of men is what made Ananias lie.

verseByVerse.quote: But a man named Ananias, with his wife Sapphira, sold a piece of property, and with his wife's knowledge he kept back for himself some of the proceeds and brought only a part of it and laid it at the apostles' feet.
verseByVerse.commentary:
But a man named Ananias, with his wife Sapphira, also sold a piece of property. With his wife’s full knowledge he kept back part of the money for himself, but brought the rest and put it at the apostles’ feet.

But. The contrast with Barnabas (4:36–37).

Kept back. Nosphizomai: embezzled, pilfered. The same rare word the Greek Old Testament uses of Achan, who secretly took plunder devoted to God when Israel entered Canaan: “the people of Israel broke faith in regard to the devoted things” (Joshua 7:1). At the beginning of the conquest and at the beginning of the church, hidden greed is exposed.

With his wife’s knowledge. A shared plan. Marriages can conspire in sin as well as encourage holiness.

On a Tuesday. Couples: do you encourage each other to honesty, or help each other hide things?

parallels.desc: Achan keeps back what was devoted to God

verseByVerse.quote: But Peter said, "Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit and to keep back for yourself part of the proceeds of the land? While it remained unsold, did it not remain your own? And after it was sold, was it not at your disposal? Why is it that you have contrived this deed in your heart?
